title: I wanted to make a character walk. Ended up building a tool.
author: ananfang
selftext:
I’m building a small tactical RPG with Codex and image generation.

The character looked good. But when she walked… her feet slid, and some poses repeated.

After many tries, this worked better:

1. Play an animation on a simple 3D mannequin.
2. Capture eight frames with a fixed camera.
3. Give image generation the sheet and the original character image.
4. Ask it to convert each frame into the character’s appearance.
5. Play it at the original timing and check it on the map.

My learning: **give it a clearer reference, instead of more instructions.**

Our walk and breathing idle look good now. Still need to check each result, though.

I turned the guide-making part into a free, open-source browser tool  
[https://ananfang.github.io/training-grounds/](https://ananfang.github.io/training-grounds/)

All this, because I wanted her to walk. 🚶🏻

Has anyone tried a similar approach?

comments.author: DaneBl
comments.body: Using the mannequin as the motion reference is a neat workaround. How much of the foot sliding disappeared with the eight-frame sheet, and how much still needed timing cleanup once it was back on the map?
